import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Filter out near-duplicates based on correlation
    ids = list(feats.ids)
    types = list(feats.types)
    x = feats.x
    y = feats.y
    
    # Compute correlations
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(x.T)
    to_remove = set()
    for i in range(len(ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= 0.6:
                to_remove.add(j)
    
    # Keep only unique features
    keep = [i for i in range(len(ids)) if i not in to_remove]
    filtered_ids = [ids[i] for i in keep]
    filtered_x = x[:, keep]
    
    # Select top features by t-statistic
    t_stats = []
    for i in range(len(filtered_ids)):
        group0 = filtered_x[y==0, i]
        group1 = filtered_x[y==1, i]
        t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(group0, group1, equal_var=False)
        t_stats.append(abs(t_stat))
    
    # Sort by t-statistic
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(t_stats)[::-1]
    top_features = [filtered_ids[i] for i in sorted_indices[:MAX_DRIVERS]]
    
    # Check if any features have strong effect
    if not top_features or max(t_stats) < 5.0:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Build design
    drivers = tuple(top_features[:min(MAX_DRIVERS, len(top_features))])
    columns = tuple(filtered_ids)
    
    # Add product terms between top features
    products = []
    for i in range(len(top_features)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(top_features)):
            a, b = top_features[i], top_features[j]
            if abs(corr_matrix[ids.index(a), ids.index(b)]) < 0.6:
                products.append((a, b))
    
    # Weighted score using top features
    loadings = {fid: t_stats[sorted_indices[ids.index(fid)]] 
                for fid in top_features}
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
